learning_outcomes.text: Applies the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids.
Designs structural elements according to appropriate codes.
Determines stresses and deformations in the elastic field generated in a solid as a result of external loads.

Identifies and analyzes the loads and stress states to which structures and mechanical systems are subjected. Analyzes and calculates structural elements according to stiffness and strength criteria. Analyzes the stress and deformation state using numerical methods.

syllabus_topics: General Theory of Bending: stress analysis. Definitions.
Navier's law for calculating normal stresses in pure bending.
Sizing of bars in simple bending.
General Theory of Bending: deformation analysis. Definitions.
Double integration method for calculating deflections.
Application to the calculation of hyperstatic beams.
Skew Bending and Combined Bending. Definitions.
Torsion. Torsion in straight bars and of circular section.
Combined actions. Calculation and design of elements subjected to combined actions.
teaching_methods: General description of the course organization, working methods, and evaluation methods.
Resolution by the student of complex problems applying theoretical and practical concepts. The student will submit a written document with the resolution of the posed problem that will be evaluable.
Development of the main theoretical concepts using ICT techniques and blackboard.
Practical exposition of the concepts acquired in the master classes through the resolution of practical problems.
Resolution by the student of simple problems applying the most basic theoretical and practical concepts. This will be done with virtual platforms like Moodle.
Resolution of doubts and explanation of misunderstood concepts.

assessment_methods.method: Problem Based Learning (PBL) / Problem Based Learning (ABP)

assessment_rules: The minimum grade for the second development test (second partial exam) is 3 to be able to average with other continuous assessment tests. To pass the course in continuous assessment, the student must have completed all required evaluative activities during the course. An average grade equal to or greater than 4 between the two partials is also required. In the second call, the student will be examined on the global content of the course in a single exam, which constitutes 100% of the grade. Fraudulent use of any means in evaluative activities will result in a failing grade for that activity.
